title: You Can Now Verify Your Facebook Account With a Video Selfie
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 24, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Facebook is adding a free verification feature that allows users to upload a selfie video and earn a white check mark.
                                            This is a separate feature from Meta Verified, which is a paid subscription for obtaining a blue check mark in Facebook and Instagram.
                                            You'll record a short selfie video, which Facebook will compare to other profile photos, but you should consider whether you want to provide more data to Meta.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you're on Facebook, you may soon see a new type of verification badge on user profiles meant to indicate that there is a real, live person behind them. The platform is adding a free verification feature that allows users to upload a selfie video and earn a white check mark, which will appear on their profile and across Marketplace, Dating, and Groups. (At launch, badges won't appear in Feed posts, but Facebook says that feature will be added in the future.)Note that this is different from Meta Verified, a paid subscription that provides the blue check mark to accounts on Facebook and Instagram. This verification indicates that Meta has confirmed the user's identity based on a review of their government-issued ID and, in some cases, a selfie video. How Facebook Verified worksFacebook Verified is available to users age 18 and older whose accounts are in good standing with the platform's community standards, though the feature is launching in select markets initially before being rolled out globally. Once you have access, you'll need to record a short video selfie, which Facebook will compare to existing profile photos on your account using facial recognition. If your verification is approved, the white check mark will be added to your profile. Verification is not available for Pages or ProMode accounts. 
Consider your privacy firstFacebook says it will store your selfie video for "up to 30 days" after verification, which is a one-time process. It's not entirely clear what happens with that video in the meantime, and it's worth noting that Meta has relied on user data to train its AI. Meta AI (and Meta more broadly) is a terrible offender when it comes to privacy and security, so you should consider whether the tradeoff of a verification mark is worth handing over more of your data and read the privacy policy before you agree. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Google also launched a video selfie verification feature this week, though its purpose is to prove your identity should you get locked out of your account. Unlike Facebook Verified, which is meant to be a trust signal to other users, Google's selfie verification allows access to your entire Google account, bringing with it some additional security considerations.

title: Scammers Are Impersonating Spotify to Steal Your Credit Card Info
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise

        July 28, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: 	Chris McGrath / Getty Images News via Getty Inages
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Scammers love to impersonate trusted brands—ranging from big tech names like Microsoft and Google to password managers and payment apps—in their phishing campaigns to lure their marks, and their latest guise is Spotify. A new email is circulating alerting users to supposed payment issues, prompting them to hand over their credit card details and Spotify login credentials. Phishing emails use Spotify brandingAs The Guardian reports, Spotify users have received messages with the subject line "review billing info" claiming that the platform "encountered an issue while processing your recent payment." Recipients are urged to "review and update" their information to keep their accounts active. The button in the email directs users to a spoofed website, where users are prompted to enter their username and password, followed by their credit card number, address, and phone number—everything scammers need to make fraudulent purchases. One victim reported seeing a suspicious charge for more than $600 within minutes of handing over their information. The emails closely replicate Spotify's branding, including its colors and logo, and appear to come from a sender called MySpotify. The fraudulent website also looks convincing at first glance. However, unlike some of the more sophisticated phishing schemes that exploit vulnerabilities in order to use real domains (like Google and PayPal), this one from Spotify breaks down when you look closer. 
For one, both the sender's address and the website URL clearly are not connected to spotify.com or any legitimate subdomain. The subject line is all lowercase, and there are no specifics about users' subscriptions or accounts in the email body. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
How to avoid getting scammed by Spotify impersonatorsPayment issues are a common scam tactic, and you should always be skeptical of any communication that urges you to provide or update banking or credit card info (or sends you to a login page along the way, which is designed to harvest your credentials). If you receive a notification from Spotify about failed payments, don't click links, download attachments, or reply. Spotify won't request payment info, passwords, or other sensitive information over email.If you're concerned about a payment or subscription problem, go directly to your account in the Spotify app or a web browser instead. If you've already entered your Spotify credentials into a suspicious site, change your password and keep an eye on your credit card transactions to catch any fraudulent charges. You can also forward phishing emails to [email protected].

title: It Just Got a Lot Cheaper to Try Gemini Spark, Google's AI Agent
body:
Pranay Parab
                            
        
            Pranay Parab
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperiencePranay Parab is an independent tech journalist based in Mumbai, India. He covers tech for Lifehacker, and specializes in tutorials and in-depth features.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 24, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Google
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Gemini Spark, the AI agent built into Google Gemini, is now a lot cheaper to try out in the U.S. Previously, Gemini Spark was exclusive to the Google AI Ultra plan, which costs $100-$200 per month. The company is now bringing the agentic AI to its AI Pro plan, which costs $20 per month. (For now, this change is exclusive to the U.S.)When Gemini Spark was announced during Google I/O 2026, its features seemed potentially useful, but the barrier to entry was too high for most people. That appears to be changing now, as Google has cut the price by as much as 90%. It is not yet available on the $5/month AI Plus plan or the free tier, but that could change in the future too—though it's likely that using Gemini Spark on lower pricing tiers could mean that you hit your usage limits much faster.What is Gemini Spark?Google Gemini is a chatbot and a voice assistant that answers your questions, creates text, media, and even entire apps for you. Gemini Spark takes those capabilities to your Google account and executes actions for you.
You can think of Gemini Spark as a personal AI assistant that can look at your emails, calendar entries, photos, and other data in your Google account to perform tasks on your behalf. You can use Spark to bulk unsubscribe from mailing lists, make flight bookings, send reminder emails to clients, colleagues, or family members, book appointments, and much more. Having said all that, a Gemini Spark overview from out sister site PC Mag emphasizes that its features tend to overlap with Gemini. PC Mag called Spark the best AI agent yet, but that doesn't mean it's perfect.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Does Gemini Spark respect your privacy?To someone who is even remotely privacy-conscious, using Gemini Spark is going to sound quite invasive: You basically have to give it access to your entire computer if you want it to be able to act on your behalf. Google is aware of that, and has programmed the AI agent to ask for confirmations before performing certain actions. If you ask the agent to find birthday photos from 2017 and email them to someone, for example, Gemini Spark will show you the pictures and ask for a confirmation before actually sending the email. It applies the same logic to deleting emails, sending messages, using your saved credit cards to pay for reservations, and more.It's worth keeping in mind that AI services have created serious problems for people who use these apps without due caution. The biggest strength of Gemini is its access to all the data that’s in your Google account, but if you give it unrestricted access and the AI agent messes up a request, you could be stuck with an incorrect hotel reservation, a flight booked to a wrong country, or other serious consequences.

title: 10 Hacks Every Google Drive User Should Know
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        August 4, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: René Ramos/Lifehacker/Google/Adobe Stock
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        As the hub for (almost) all files stored in your Google Account, Drive is a critical tool for Workspace users to save, organize, and share documents, spreadsheets, and media. To keep your Drive organized and make the most of its collaboration features, use these 10 hidden hacks.  Add shortcuts instead of duplicating files to save storage spaceIf you're organizing Drive and need a single file to be accessible from multiple folders—such as across several projects—you don't need to move it or create multiple copies, which takes up storage space and prevents collaborators across separate teams from working in the same live version. Instead, leave the original where it is and create shortcuts in other locations. Right-click on any Drive file to bring up the options menu, then go to Organize > Add shortcut and select the destination folder. Use URL shortcuts to quickly create account-specific new filesURL shortcuts are huge timesavers for launching new Drive files—Docs, Sheets, and Slides specifically—especially if you're logged into multiple Google Accounts, such as work and personal, at the same time. When you type doc.new, sheet.net, or slide.new into your address bar, a new file will automatically be created under your primary account. Add /1, /2, /3 etc. to specify which account you want to use. This prevents multiple clicks just to get a new file started. 
Another URL shortcut allows you to force shared file recipients to create a copy rather than gaining view or edit access to the original. This is handy for sharing templates, checklists, and other materials that users will need to edit while preserving the master version. Simply replace /edit or /view at the end of the sharing link with /copy, and recipients will be prompted to "Make a Copy" upon opening. Upload new versions to overwrite existing docs without changing the sharing linkNative Google files update in real time when edited, allowing all collaborators to see changes, but new versions of PDFs, images, and videos have to be reshared—unless you overwrite the original. Right-click on any non-Google file and go to Manage versions > Upload new version to keep the same sharing link for the update. Lock files in read-only mode to prevent further editsIf you want to share the final version of a Drive file but prevent recipients from making edits—either accidentally or on purpose—you can lock it in read-only mode. This is quicker than turning it into a PDF or managing permissions for different users. Right-click on the file to pull up the options menu, then go to File information > Lock. (Note that you will also be unable to make edits until you unlock the file.) Enable upload conversions to make .docx files into compatible Google filesAnother feature that saves a few clicks is auto-conversion of external files into Google formats. This is especially useful if you frequently receive documents from Microsoft users in .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx formats. Instead of manually converting each time, go to Settings > General, scroll down to Uploads, and toggle on Convert uploads to Google Docs editor format. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Editable Drive files allow you to easily highlight and leave comments on text, but you can do the same for other files while in preview mode, which is useful for providing feedback on visuals, layouts and design without downloading and opening in a separate program. Double-click to open any image or PDF preview and tap the Comment icon at the top. Select the area you want to leave feedback on and add your comment. Use advanced search operators to quickly find buried filesMy personal Drive is a bit of a mess, making it hard to find older files I've forgotten the names of without scrolling back through a very long list of unorganized items. Advanced search operators are part of the solution because they allow you to narrow down by file type, owner, and date. Enter terms like type:, owner:, and before: or after: into the search bar followed by your parameters. Drive's organizational structure is very basic—it'll show you suggested files and folders on your Home tab, but the My Drive tab is alphabetical by default with options for sorting by date modified. You can obviously create folders and move files around (including with the shortcuts hack described above), but it may also be useful to create a dynamic "hub" for quick access to files that are related, such as for a work project or a specific vacation. Paid Workspace users have a Priority tab, which collates to 25 files from anywhere in Drive without moving them from their original locations. Free users can star items or create a master Docs file and embed file tiles using the "@" menu. Use the Drive scanner to quickly digitize receipts and printed documents You don't actually need yet another app for document scanning: Google Drive has that feature built in, so both iPhone and Android users can quickly digitize printed material to Drive simply by using their device's camera. Open the Drive app and select the Scan icon or the (+), then hit Scan document. Google will make minor enhancements, then you can select the name and destination and hit Upload. From there, your scanned receipts, contracts, and other files are searchable just like anything else in your Drive.

title: Nano Banana 2 Is Coming to Google Earth
body:
David Nield
                            
        
            David Nield
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceDavid Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years. He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 30, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Google
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Google Earth is getting a Nano Banana 2 upgrade.
                                            With it, you can create futuristic vistas or dive back into the historic past of a place.
                                            The update is rolling out now for all Google Earth users on the web.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Known by the codename Nano Banana 2, the most recent AI image generation updates added to Google Gemini have been a significant step forward in terms of quality and accuracy, and now similar capabilities are being plugged into the Google Earth app on the web. It means you're able to use the aerial, satellite, and 3D imagery packed into Google Earth as the basis for prompts for AI images—maybe peering into the distant past with a historical reconstruction or looking to the future with a sci-fi reimagining.We've already seen just how precise and realistic the Nano Banana-powered features in Google Gemini are now, and Google has five suggestions for how you might deploy these capabilities in Google Earth. First, you can learn while exploring, so maybe getting the AI to build an infographic on the Statue of Liberty with key historical facts about it.
    
            
            One idea for the new feature: Infographics (the Statue of Liberty in this case).
                                        Credit: Google
                    
    
A text prompt such as "reimagine this empty lot in Tokyo as a vibrant shopping and retail district with open spaces" would transform a rather bare part of the Google Earth 3D map into something quite different. You can also visualize personal projects such as a dream lakeside home or an extension for your current property. Google Earth would combine the existing landscape with whatever you prompted, and help you come up with ideas as part of the planning stage.
You can also look forwards and backwards. "Sometimes it’s fun to let your imagination run wild," says Google, suggesting that you might want to get the AI to imagine how a place might look in a hundred years. (It might be worth nudging your prompt towards a utopian rather than dystopian vision of the future.)Finally, Google suggests you dive back into the past. The company showcased a demo with the prompt "render a hyper-realistic view of what these Pompeii ruins looked like in 78 AD," which could be used by teachers, for example. That would instantly transform today's ruins "into a bustling, colorful street scene from the Roman Empire," in Google's words.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
These new features come with the usual AI image caveats, however. While Nano Banana 2 can pull real-world information and images from the web, and is able to render graphics with more consistency and accuracy than previous models, there's still going to be the usual weaknesses involved with AI: Your lakeside home might not be entirely structurally sound, and the Pompeii reconstruction may not be entirely authentic—so bear that in mind when your images are produced.
    
            
            Pompeii in all its original glory, as depicted by AI. 
                                        Credit: Google
                    
    
When I asked Google about this, a representative emphasized the real-world knowledge base that Nano Banana 2 draws on, which includes all the text and graphics it can find online, as well as the vast number of images that have been plugged into the AI during its training. With Google Earth, it will also trace over the structure ruins that are still in place when it comes to Pompeii, for example.For a bit more clarity, you can try quizzing the Nano Banana 2 model inside the main Gemini app: I got it to render an imagined scene from Pompeii just prior to it being smothered by Vesuvius, then asked about the image accuracy. The AI said it had combined a bunch of real, historical information points to render the scene, including details on Pompeii's raised sidewalks, and the clothing styles of the day. Google hasn't said anything specific about usage limits, but the Nano Banana 2 upgrade is rolling out now globally, for all users of Google Earth on the web.

                What do you think so far?
            
        

    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

The company claimed the outage did not stem from a cyberattack, rather a software issue. We don't know why T-Mobile is down at the moment, but, in all likelihood, the company will update the public sooner than later, if not fix the issue altogether.

title: How to Stop Scammers From Showing You Ads on Your Android After Every Phone Call
body:
Emily Long
                            
        
            Emily Long
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperienceEmily Long is a freelance writer based in Salt Lake City. After graduating from Duke University, she spent several years reporting on the federal workforce for Government Executive, a publication of Atlantic Media Company, in Washington, D.C. She has nearly a decade of experience as a freelancer covering tech (including issues related to security, privacy, and streaming) as well as personal finance and travel. In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 29, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Bloomberg / Contributor via Getty Images
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        If you're an Android user who is seeing ads pop up after your phone calls, you need not assume this is some new feature you have to learn to live with. It's actually an ad fraud scam, and you can do something about it. Researchers have identified dozens of apps on the Google Play Store that are able to display ads on top of the Android phone interface, a scheme known as AfterCall. How ads are taking over Android callsThis scam originates with seemingly harmless utility apps downloaded from the Google Play Store, such as calendars, alarm clocks, and notepads. When installed, they request overlay permissions, which allow them to appear on top of other apps—and thus display ads over phone calls. These apps can detect when a call ends and will then launch full-screen ads wrapped in a fake call info screen. Since it looks like they are simply part of the call interface, users may be less likely to suspect that they are actually malicious. It's worth noting that overlay permissions can't be granted via a standard pop-up during the app installation process. They are a type of "special permission" that requires users to go into their system settings to enable. Android apps are supposed to request these permissions in context and give a clear reason for doing so. AfterCall scammers are using justifications like alarms not being able to go off or appear correctly without overlay permissions, though some apps will simply crash if users decline permissions.
How to remove AfterCall adsBecause the ads appear out of context—after a phone call and with content unrelated to the utility app—it's harder for users to figure out what's causing them. The utility apps aren't obviously malicious and don't appear on recent app lists when ads are displayed, so it's not obvious that they are connected to the problem. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
If you are seeing ads pop up after phone calls on your Android, check for apps that have overlay permissions. Go to Settings > Apps > Special app access (this may be hidden behind a three-dot menu) and click on the permission type. Look for apps you don't recognize, or which shouldn't have "display on top" permissions, and uninstall them. You should regularly audit these permissions, and disable any that aren't essential. On the user side, these apps seem to be mostly an annoyance rather than outright malicious programs that are harvesting your sensitive data, though installing any program that requests unnecessary permissions can introduce significant risk. If nothing else, however, these apps do appear to waste brands' advertising dollars and could damage their reputation with users—but you probably just care about how to stop seeing them after your calls.

title: The Pixel 11's Biggest New Feature Might Be Its Inflated Price Tag
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 30, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: picture alliance / Contributor via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Rumors suggest Google is adding small upgrades to the Pixel 11 series, such as new Tensor chips and camera sensors.
                                            However, the biggest change might be the Pixel 11 series' bigger price tag when compared to the Pixel 10.
                                            Google may drop the 128GB base model for the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro, which would effectively raise the entry price by $100.
                                            The Pixel 11 Pro XL and 11 Pro Fold may receive a price hike for no other reason than the ongoing memory crisis.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Smartphone manufacturers rarely innovate these days, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. It's a sign that iPhones and Androids have gotten so good, there's little room left for major advancements and upgrades. When a company like Google announces a new smartphone line, most of us aren't expecting something that will convince us to upgrade from its previous generation; rather, you know that if it's time to buy a new phone, the latest generation will likely be the de facto "best" phone you can buy.   So it seems is the case for Google's upcoming Pixel 11 lineup. Rumors suggest that the company is making small updates in some key areas as you might expect, without changing too much from the Pixel 10. The biggest change, it seems, might just be the phone's price tag. If you're considering upgrading to a new Pixel 11 device, know you might just be paying more for it than ever.
What's new with the Pixel 11As highlighted by Engadget, the overall design of the Pixel 11 line is virtually identical to the Pixel 10. That goes for all rumored models, including the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and the Pixel 11 Pro Fold. If you have a corresponding Pixel 10 device, the Pixel 11 upgrade will have the same screen sizes, which means the lineup will have the following displays:
Pixel 11: 6.3-inches (1080 x 2424)Pixel 11 Pro: 6.3-inches (1280 x 2856)Pixel 11 Pro XL: 6.8-inches (1344 x 2992)Pixel 11 Pro Fold: 6.3-inch outer display (1080 x 2342) and 8-inch inner display (2076 x 2160)The camera bumps will remain unchanged as well, though the hardware itself may get a bit of an upgrade. The Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold may ship with 50 MP main cameras, which is a slight bump up from the 48 MP camera on the Pixel 10. The cameras on the 11 Pro and 11 Pro XL may get new sensors as well. While it might seem like you wouldn't be able to tell the difference between the Pixel 11 and Pixel 10 by sight alone, you actually will. That's because the rumors suggest Google will introduce new colors for the lineup. The Pixel 11 may ship in Midnight, Fuchsia, and Moss, while the Pixel 11 Pro may come in Dune, Pine, and Sterling. Finally, the Pixel 11 Pro may ship in Midnight or Pine.   Perhaps the biggest upgrade this year will be the Tensor G6 chip. Engadget says that Google's latest SoC (System-on-a-Chip) is built on a 2nm process, which may be the same as Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 series. While we'll need access to the phone for actual benchmarking and real-world tests, the new chip could offer better battery life and power efficiency than the current Tensor G5.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
The Pixel 11 may be more expensive than everHowever, new chips are expected with new smartphone generations. Perhaps the biggest shock this year will be how much you actually have to pay to acquire Google's newest phones. Like Apple, Google may drop the 128GB base model options for the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro, and may instead choose to start at 256GB. While that's good for users who often run out of storage, it takes away the previous base model price tag of $799. Now, the new entry price will be $899: technically the same price, but it will cost $100 more to get a new Pixel than it used to. The Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold, however, may just get a price increase for no other reason than the ongoing memory crisis. Because of sharp demand for RAM and other computer components across the globe, companies are raising prices across the board. As such, Engadget suggests that the Pixel 11 Pro XL and Pixel 11 Pro Fold may get a €100 increase, which could reflect a $100 increase in the U.S. as well.        If you need the latest and greatest from Google for your next phone, you'll have no choice but to spend the extra money. However, you might be better off finding a good deal on a Pixel 10 or a Pixel 10a. After all, there's not that much difference between the Pixel 11 series to necessarily justify the rumored price increase.

title: 10 Snipping Tool Hacks Every Windows 11 User Should Know
body:
Pranay Parab
                            
        
            Pranay Parab
                
                                                                        Freelance Writer
                                                            
            
            
        
            ExperiencePranay Parab is an independent tech journalist based in Mumbai, India. He covers tech for Lifehacker, and specializes in tutorials and in-depth features.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 31, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Ian Moore/Lifehacker/Adobe Stock/Microsoft
                            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Snipping Tool is the default app for screenshots in Windows 11. There's a lot more to the app than that, however: With it, you can take screen recordings, extract text from images or websites that disable copying, and use a reverse image search tool. While ShareX is still my favorite app for taking screenshots in Windows, I think Snipping Tool has reached a point where it's great for both beginners and power users. Here are 10 essential Snipping Tool hacks that every Windows 11 user should know.Use 'Scan Text' to copy text from imagesCopying text from images is one of the most common uses of screenshot tools, and Snipping Tool does it quite well. You can right-click any image in Windows 11, and go to Open with > Snipping Tool. Once the photo opens, you can click the Scan Text button to select all the text in the image. Windows will take a few moments to identify all the text in the photo, and, when it's ready, you can click Copy all text from the popover menu. You're also free to select a single sentence or block of text by clicking and dragging the cursor over it, and you can right-click this selection to reveal the Copy text button.If all you want to do is copy text from sites that disable copying, interface elements in an app, or PDFs of scanned pages where you can't select the text easily, then you should use Snipping Tool to select and copy text without even taking a screenshot. This allows you to reduce unwanted image clutter by skipping the "taking a screenshot" step, and jumping straight to extracting text. To try this, open the Snipping Tool app in your Windows PC, and click the Text extractor button in the toolbar. You can click and drag over an area of the screen that contains text, and the app will automatically select it in a moment or two. Click Copy all text in the popover menu, and you're done.
Use this setting to automatically redact sensitive information from screenshots
    
            
            
                                        Credit: Pranay Parab
                    
    
Snipping Tool allows you to do some basic image editing, which you can use to automatically redact sensitive information from screenshots. Open any screenshot in Snipping Tool, and click Scan text. Once the tool scans for text, a popover menu will appear. You can select Quick redact here to automatically hide all phone numbers and email addresses in the screenshot. It's pretty accurate and puts a black bar over sensitive information, which is much safer than blurring phone numbers and email addresses.Use the timer to set up your screen before taking screenshotsSetting up an elaborate screenshot on your PC can be frustrating since Snipping Tool takes the screenshot instantly by default. In these instances, you can set a delay of three to 10 seconds before you capture the screen. If you have the Snipping Tool open, right-click its icon in the taskbar to quickly take a timed screenshot. Three buttons let you take a screenshot in three, five, or 10 seconds. You can also set up the Snipping Tool to always add a delay before capturing a screenshot. Open the app, and click the camera icon in the toolbar. Then, click the timer icon in the toolbar, and select the delay you wish to add.Use Snipping Tool for screencasts to help others solve tech issuesWhen my friends or family members call for help with tech issues, I often send them a screencast with commentary to show how to fix the issue. In Snipping Tool, you can toggle a setting to include microphone audio by default when you record the screen. This lets me record my voice while I'm demonstrating how to solve the problem, and I use the mouse pointer to highlight what to click. Once you set up Snipping Tool to record your audio by default for screen recordings, this process hardly takes any time. Open Snipping Tool in your PC, and click the three-dots icon in the top-right corner. Select Settings, and enable Include microphone input by default when a screen recording starts.
    
            
            
                                        Credit: Pranay Parab
                    
    
When you capture screenshots, you can make Snipping Tool automatically add a solid color border to each image. This is great for posting to social media, as it makes screenshots look uniform and fit your aesthetic. Go to Snipping Tool settings and enable Add border to each screenshot. Select the Color block to pick the color you want for the border, and use the Thickness slider to adjust the width of the border.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Use the Freeform tool to capture screenshots in irregular shapesThe Freeform tool lets you draw an area on the screen, and captures a screenshot of everything inside that area. You can draw any shape you like, and the tool automatically closes small gaps in the shape to complete the screenshot. I like the fact that the Freeform tool is forgiving enough to smooth out poorly drawn shapes, which means you don't necessarily need to have steady hands to capture useful screenshots. To use this tool, open Snipping Tool, and click the camera icon in the toolbar. Next, select the rectangle icon, and choose Freeform. When you take the next screenshot, Snipping Tool will let you draw an irregular shape on the screen.Disable automatic saving to stop screenshots from piling up on your PCIf you disable auto-save for screenshots, it directly copies screenshots to the clipboard. You can then make edits and send them to the app you need, or hit the save button to store the edited screenshots. This stops screenshots from piling up and adding to the clutter on your hard drive. I only need to save around one in 10 screenshots I capture, which makes this particularly useful for me. To try it out, go to Snipping Tool settings and disable Automatically save original screenshots.Use this tool to hide people's faces from photos or screenshotsSnipping Tool has a "Shapes" option, which is meant to hide people's faces from images or screenshots. Here's how it works: Once you open an image in Snipping Tool, you'll see a bunch of editing tools in the toolbar. Select the Shapes tool, which is next to the Eraser tool, and you'll see a series of options. Select the Emoji tool to add an emoticon over faces. Alternatively, you can select the Square or Oval tools, but be sure to use the color fill option to hide private information thoroughly. Select Fill, and choose a color. You can also disable the Outline if you wish to, as it adds a border to the shape you draw on the screenshot. Then, you can draw a rectangle, square, circle, or an oval on the screenshot, and you'll find a solid color block that can hide sensitive information.Use the built-in reverse image search to identify objects in the screenshotsSnipping Tool has a reverse image search feature that uses Bing to locate objects, places, or elements from your screenshots or images. You can use this to identify subjects in an image, or to check if a scammer has copied a profile picture from a different person's profile. To use this feature, open an image in Snipping Tool, and click the three dots in the top-right corner of the app. Select Visual Search with Bing, and it will open Bing's reverse image search results in your default browser.

title: Microsoft and Amazon Are Both Introducing New Cloud Gaming Options
body:
Stephen Johnson
                            
        
            Stephen Johnson
                
                                            Senior Staff Writer
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceStephen Johnson is a senior staff writer at Lifehacker covering pop culture and technology, including the columns “The Out-of-Touch Adults’ Guide to Kid Culture” and “What People Are Getting Wrong This Week.”
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 27, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    We may earn a commission from links on this page.
    
            Credit: Microsoft
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            Microsoft is testing a free, ad-supported cloud gaming tier for Xbox Insiders.
                                            Amazon is integrating its Luna cloud gaming service directly into Prime Video for Fire TV users.
                                            Both options are available now.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Two tech giants, Microsoft and Amazon, took steps last week to move gaming further into the cloud, with each company aiming at a different part of the (gigantic) gaming demographic.  Microsoft is testing a free (albeit ad-supported) cloud-gaming model for Xbox games. Starting today, gamers who signed up for Microsoft's Xbox Insider Program will be able to play games from their library that are cloud-compatible, without paying for a Game Pass Ultimate subscription. They will, however, have to watch ads at the beginning of the session. Microsoft is currently capping playtime at one hour per session; use up your time and you'll have to watch more ads. There's no word yet on how long the test will be running. Amazon is embedding games on Fire productsMeanwhile, Amazon announced it is going to embed its Luna cloud gaming service directly into Prime Video—but only if you have a Fire TV device. Fire TV users will see a dedicated "Games" tab next to "Movies," "TV shows" and "Sports." They will be able to play titles like Hogwarts Legacy, EA Sports FC 26 and Clue for the cost of their Prime membership. 
The two companies clearly have different targets in mind. Microsoft is catering to the kind of "core" gamers who already own a library of titles but might want to play them on secondary devices like phones and laptops. Amazon is going after more casual gamers, and is trying to put their gaming offerings in front of as many eyeballs as possible. It plans to package its games on the same pages as the movie entries for well-known IP like Harry Potter, so someone might decide to play a little game with their remote before they watch a movie.If you have an Xbox, here's how to check out some ad-supported cloud gaming. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
Download the Xbox Insider Hub app on Xbox Series X|S, Xbox One, or Windows PC.Enroll in the Xbox Insider Program. It's free. That's it! Now you can stream select cloud-compatible games you own (after you check out some commercials, of course.)How to check out Amazon's Luna gaming serviceIf you have Prime, you can already try Luna. The company isn't adding any extra content for Fire TV users; it's just changing the way it presents the games it offers. Here's how to check it out. First, you'll need a n Amazon Fire device. That means Fire TV stick, Fire TV Cube, or a smart TV running the Fire TV operating system.On the main menu, you should see the new "Games" tab.Click it and go to town. Pro tip: Play Indiana Jones and the Great Circle because it is fantastic. You can play Luna games with any Bluetooth controller or use your phone as the controller.

        While you might know Dyson for leading the charge in the best vacuum cleaners and air purifiers, the high-tech home brand also offers some of the best over-ear headphones on the market, with a fun, flashy look. After a polarizing initial headphones debut with a built-in air filter, the noise-canceling Dyson OnTrac headphones are a successful follow-up with superb sound quality, and right now, they’re at an all-time low: 50% off, down to $249 (originally $499).
Available in CNC Aluminum and CNC copper, these stylish aluminum headphones have a retro-futuristic vibe similar to Nothing’s over-ear headphones. They earned an "Excellent" rating from PCMag for their impressive sound quality, bolstered by strong bass and mids, as well as superior noise cancellation. They feature plush foam cushioning on the earcups and headband for extended listening, with hinges that allow them to fold flat and fit in their included case. Controls live on a raised mount attached to the headband and are less finicky than touch panels.   Battery life lasts up to 55 hours with ANC, plus nine hours from a 30-minute charge, easily surpassing top contenders like the Bose QuietComfort, Sony WH-1000XM5, and AirPods Max, making them a solid choice for long flights or anyone who often forgets to charge their headphones. They connect to the MyDyson app, which also controls the brand’s other devices. While there are three equalizer modes and three noise-cancellation modes, there’s no custom EQ. That said, the app does have one unique feature: Sound exposure metrics monitor whether you’re exposed to unsafe sound levels over time.
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
The ANC also competes with top models from brands like Sony and Bose, muffling both low and high frequencies with ease. The bass is thunderous, sound doesn’t distort even at high volume, and mic quality is strong for voice calls. If you enjoy the OnTrac aesthetic, want a heavy dose of bass with your listening experience, and battery life that’s hard to beat, you won’t be disappointed by the Dyson OnTrac headphones, especially at a rare 50% discount.

title: Your Samsung Galaxy Watch's Browser Just Got a Useful Upgrade
body:
Jake Peterson
                            
        
            Jake Peterson
                
                                            Senior Technology Editor
                                    
            
            
        
            ExperienceJake Peterson is Lifehacker’s Tech Editor, and has been covering tech news and how-tos for nearly a decade. His team covers all things technology, including AI, smartphones, computers, game consoles, and subscriptions.
        
        
            Areas of Expertise
        
        Read Full Bio
    

    
                                        
        
        
        July 31, 2026
                
        Add as a preferred source on Google

    
    
        Add as a preferred source on Google

            Credit: Bloomberg / Contributor via Getty Images
                            
            
                Key Takeaways
                                            If you have a Galaxy Watch, the latest version of Samsung Browser is a bit more like a desktop web browser than before.
                                            Once you update your browser, you'll be able to download images from webpages directly to your watch.
                                            There are limited supported file types, and the image needs to be 10MB or smaller.
                                    
            
    Table of Contents
    
        
        Full disclosure: I'm all-in on the Apple ecosystem, and I don't necessarily plan to switch anytime soon—but that doesn't mean I don't peek at what could be. I have few complaints about my aging Apple Watch, but, I'll admit, Android smartwatches can be pretty cool. While I don't think I'd be doing a whole lot of web browsing on my watch, the fact that the Galaxy Watch has a dedicated browser is a great feature. (For the uninitiated: Apple Watches have a built-in web browser that only appears when watchOS deems a search relevant. There is no Safari app for the Apple Watch.)If you have a Galaxy Watch, you probably already know you can install Samsung Browser on your device. What you might not know, however, is that your wearable web browser just got an excellent upgrade that makes it function even more like a desktop web browser. As reported by SamMobile, Samsung Browser for Galaxy Watch now lets you download images from webpages. That means if you stumble across a picture on the web, you can download it directly to your Galaxy Watch, rather than switch to your phone, tablet, or computer to save it.How to download images on your Galaxy Watch's Samsung BrowserFirst, update Samsung Browser to its latest version, then open it and navigate to a webpage of your choosing. When you find an image you want to download, long-press on the image, and you'll see a new "Download Image" option. Tap it, and your image will save on your watch. You can find all downloaded images in the "Downloads" folder on the Samsung Browser home page. 
SamMobile notes that this option doesn't seem to work until the website has fully loaded. As such, you may need to wait a bit longer than you might expect before you're able to download an image. In addition, there are some limitations: You can download PNG, JPEG, JPG, and GIFs up to 10MB. If you come across a different file type, or the image in question is too large, you won't be able to download it. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
This should work on any Galaxy Watch that can run the latest version of Samsung Browser. However, if you're in the market for an upgrade, Samsung recently announced the Galaxy Watch 9 at its July Unpacked event. The watch is due out Aug. 7, so you can preorder it now or wait until it comes out to see if older Galaxy Watches come down in price.

    Table of Contents
    
        
        There are all kinds of robot lawn mowers, but finding one that can effectively handle a moderately large lawn with complicated terrain can be tricky. If you live on a property with trees, slopes, narrow passages, or weak GPS reception, you likely need a model that can handle the above with autonomous LiDAR-and-camera mapping. The MOVA LiDAX Ultra 3000 robot mower is a reliable option, and it's currently $800 off, down to an all-time low price of $2,199.
This AI-enabled mower has four-motor AWD and a wide dual-disc deck, running without a perimeter wire or RTK antenna. A physical bumper, dual 1080p cameras, and LiDAR offer three layers of obstacle detection. Runtime is up to 170 minutes, and it takes around an hour to charge. It can handle slopes up to 80% with an obstacle threshold height of up to 2.4 inches. It can cover up to .75 acres and has an electronically adjustable cutting height range from 1.2 to 3.9 inches, which is wider than many mowers in its class. You can set zone control for up to 150 zones and there are several mowing patterns to choose from, as well as security features like location tracking, live audio, off-map alerts, and human detection. It also lets you map out two separate areas, so you can mow both your front and back or side lawns or for two different properties, though lugging around this 52-pound beast might not be the easiest feat. It has an IPX6 rating, so it can tolerate a sprinkler going off, but may not perform ideally in the rain. 
            
                What do you think so far?
            
        
While it can easily get the job done on a flat lawn, it might be more mower than necessary. The MOVA LiDAX Ultra 3000 robot mower is really best for more challenging terrain.  Combined with a versatile cutting range, a wide range of smart features, and long battery life, this mower is a formidable player in the robot lawn mower realm and a good choice at the current 27% discount.
